reviews.review:
This game feels promising, so I am going to try to leave feedback that is as detailed as possible. 

The first few missions felt reaaaaallly slow. This may have been in part due to the length of the tutorial. In the labyrinth and battery tutorials you spend longer than necessary pushing heavy objects and just waiting for them to move, and in the spare parts tutorials, it takes way too long for the little repair drones to do their jobs. In the weapon tutorial, leaving your weapons on auto-fire leads to you running out of energy before the end, and turning off auto fire leads to getting destroyed by the big enemy before you have time to react. I feel like there should be an easy way to turn on auto-fire for all weapons or to manually fire multiple weapons at once in case of a sudden emergency, but that could also cause problems as sometimes my weapons seemed to hit my own ship, which seemed like a poorly explained mechanic. 

Prologue Mission
It feels very unpolished that the scrap pushers just despawn at the end of their track. It's clearly supposed to be an obstacle that traps you at the end, so it should look good at the end. In my opinion, several objects are too dark and seem like they could be background objects when they actually have collision (ex. the repeater towers). Crashing into one of the repeater towers and killing Shrub right before passing through a save point actually managed to softlock the game because I couldn't reactivate the station without a living human and the save happened after he had died. There were a lot of little secrets, but none of them really felt worthwhile to pick up, and it felt like stopping to explore them just made the mission take even longer with no real benefits. I was even more annoying when I decided to gather extra modules for my ship and they just ended up slamming into my ship while being pulled toward an airlock. I feel like the pulling mechanic should never pull an object with enough force to damage the object or your ship. 

This stuff may seem super nitpicky, but the tutorials and prologue are going to be most players' first experience with this game, so they really need to be a stronger starting point. I made it into the first real mission already feeling bored/burnt out, which is not a good sign. I think the prologue and tutorials could probably be condensed into one mission and streamlined to teach you the basic mechanics and story introduction more quickly, which could improve the issue of the  slow start. 

Some of the more mechanical issues I brought up could use some polish, but the idea and mechanics seems like a solid base to build off of. I will be keeping an eye on this game as it develops, and may update this review as things change. 

To the devs: Feel free to reach out if somehow this feedback wasn't already severely over-detailed, and you want even more.
reviews.developer_response:
Thanks for the detailed analysis.
Sometimes, in an effort to please everyone, a developer might try to quickly add new player wishes, but this is not the case here.
Your comments point exactly to those mechanics and aspects that we also see as needing improvement.

The game is ambitious, despite its simple appearance, and we can’t keep everything in perfect shape at the same time.
Some mechanics have simply become too familiar to us during development, so we need to step back, review them, and sometimes just remove them.

It’s a bit unfortunate that all this is happening during early access, but it’s still better that it happens now.
We’re currently gathering all feedback, especially the negative one, and using it to plan future improvements and changes.

Thank you for your time and for purchasing the game.
